layers.label: Texas Senate District
layers.rank_note: 31 Senate districts — the largest districts Texas carries below the state itself, larger on average than its 38 congressional districts

source.answers: The Texas Senate district covering the point, and the senator holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 1 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Upper), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 31 features, measured 2026-11-11. Texas's Senate districts are not built from its House districts, so each chamber's map is simplified on its own. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: tx-senate-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the Senate's own site (senate.texas.gov): the senator's name and party from each senator's own page, and the Capitol address and office telephone as printed there. The Senate links a contact form for each senator rather than an e-mail address, so none is shown. A seat the Senate marks vacant says so.

layers.label: U.S. House
layers.rank_note: 38 congressional districts — smaller on average than a Senate district

source.answers: The U.S. House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 4 (119th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 38 features for Texas, measured 2026-11-11. These are the districts the current members were elected from in 2024. The Legislature drew a new map in August 2025, and the U.S. Supreme Court let it be used for the November 2026 election, so it takes over when the current members leave office on 3 January 2027; measured that day, 37 of the 38 districts differ between the two maps, and the builder refuses to write layer 4 on or after that date. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

layers.label: Texas House District
layers.rank_note: 150 House districts — about five in each Senate district, though no rule nests them

source.answers: The Texas House district covering the point, and the member holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 2 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Lower), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 150 features, measured 2026-11-11. Simplified on its own, by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval, and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: tx-house-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the House's own site (house.texas.gov): the member's name from the House's member list and the member's own page, and the Capitol office, mailing address and telephone as printed there. Neither the House's site nor Texas Legislature Online prints a member's party or e-mail address, so neither is shown. A seat the House lists as inactive is shown as vacant.

layers.label: County
layers.rank_note: 254 counties, pre-built from TIGERweb; the instance's offline anchor layer

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 254 features, measured 2026-11-11, more counties than any other state has. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. Each Texas county is governed by a commissioners court — a county judge elected countywide and four commissioners, each elected from a commissioner precinct — and elects officers such as a sheriff and a county clerk; no list of them was read in this pass, so the card names the county only. Recorded as gap tx-county-officials.

layers.label: School District
layers.rank_note: 1,016 independent school districts, drawn from a tile archive mirrored from TIGERweb

source.answers: The public school district covering the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 0 (unified school districts), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 1,016 features for Texas, measured 2026-11-11, covering all of the state's land but one district's (Vysehrad, below).

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. Each independent school district elects a board of trustees, and no list of them was read in this pass — recorded as gap tx-school-board-members.

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 1,992 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas inside Texas (3,091 in the app's bounding box), drawn from a tile archive of the ones inside the state; the layer hides outside it

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, mirrored into a vector-tile archive of the ZCTAs inside Texas (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py). ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='48'. 3,091 features in the app's box, which reaches into the four neighbouring states and Mexico, 1,992 of them inside Texas and kept in the archive, measured 2026-11-11.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more.
source.applies: Texas. The layer is hidden outside the state outline, because outside it the Census's point query answers with a neighbouring state's real ZIP code.

layers.label: School District (Elementary)
layers.rank_note: one elementary school district, Vysehrad's, over 81.5 km2 of Lavaca County

source.answers: The elementary school district covering the point, where the Census records one.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 2 (elementary school districts), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); one feature for Texas, measured 2026-11-11: Vysehrad Independent School District in Lavaca County, which runs pre-kindergarten to grade 8 over 81.5 km2. Its older students attend Hallettsville Independent School District, which the Census records over the same ground in the secondary layer.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. Vysehrad Independent School District elects a board of trustees, and no list of them was read in this pass — recorded as gap tx-school-board-members.
source.applies: Vysehrad, in Lavaca County, only; the layer answers nothing anywhere else in Texas.

Everywhere else in Texas the Census records Hallettsville as a unified district.

layers.label: City, Town or Village
layers.rank_note: 1,230 incorporated cities, towns and villages, drawn from a tile archive mirrored from TIGERweb

source.answers: The incorporated city, town or village containing the point, or that the point is outside every one.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 4 (incorporated places), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 1,230 features for Texas, measured 2026-11-11: 978 cities, 230 towns and 22 villages, of which the Census records 3 towns as inactive governments. MOST OF TEXAS IS IN NO CITY, TOWN OR VILLAGE (4.5% of its land, 30,285.5 of 676,659.0 km2, is inside one), and there the county is the general-purpose local government, so an empty card says the point is outside every one rather than naming a place. The Census's census-designated places and county subdivisions are statistical areas with no government and are not drawn.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. No statewide roster of Texas's mayors and council members was read in this pass; the card names the place and links nothing it has not verified. Recorded as gap tx-municipal-officeholders.

layers.label: Tribal Government
layers.rank_note: Tribal land — Texas has 6 pieces held by three nations, MEASURED by scripts/build_tribal_areas.py on 2026-11-12, with the counties measured against this app's own county outlines: the Alabama-Coushatta Reservation (18.521 km²) and the Alabama-Coushatta Off-Reservation Trust Land (18.307 km² in 8 parts), both in Polk County; the Kickapoo (TX) Reservation (1.557 km² in 2 parts) and Off-Reservation Trust Land (0.133 km²), both in Maverick County; and the Ysleta del Sur Pueblo (0.299 km² in 3 parts) and the Ysleta del Sur Off-Reservation Trust Land (12.760 km² in 17 parts), both in El Paso County. Ranked after municipalities and before the point layers, as Louisiana's and Mississippi's are, so they are drawn above the larger areas around them. Drawn although no district is drawn on this land, by Adam's ruling of 2026-09-30: a government answers for that ground, so a reader who clicks it should be told which one.

source.answers: Whether this address is on tribal land, and which nation's government answers for it — Texas has 6 such areas, held by the Alabama-Coushatta Tribe of Texas, the Kickapoo Traditional Tribe of Texas and the Ysleta del Sur Pueblo.

boundary.label: US Census Bureau TIGERweb AIANNHA, current vintage — federal reservations and off-reservation trust land, shipped with the app

source.people: Each nation's council from that nation's own page, read weekly by scripts/tribal_council_scraper.py and dated on the card: the Alabama-Coushatta Tribal Council's seven members (alabama-coushatta.com; the tribe's two chiefs advise the council and are not on it), the Kickapoo Traditional Tribe of Texas's five council members (kickapootexas.org) and the Ysleta del Sur Pueblo's nine, its Governor, Lieutenant Governor, Alguacil, Cacique, War Captain and four council members (ysletadelsurpueblo.org). The government, its seat and its website come from the Bureau of Indian Affairs' tribal leaders directory (data/bia-tribal-governments.json), which lists no website for the Ysleta del Sur Pueblo; the land is joined to the government by this project's own data/tribal-government-join.json.
source.applies: Texas — the six pieces of land above, in El Paso, Maverick and Polk counties. Every other point in the state is on no tribal land the Census draws for a government.

layers.label: Police Station
layers.rank_note: nearest police stations by straight-line distance — a point layer, ranked with the other nearest-N layers

source.answers: The three nearest police stations to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader. Public domain. Measured 2026-11-11: 1,883 points in Texas's envelope, under the service's 2,000-record cap, and paged anyway so that stops being a fact anyone has to re-check.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: Texas — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in a neighbouring state, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

anchor_point.note: Texas State Capitol, 1100 Congress Avenue, Austin, Travis County

negative_point.note: The Coahuila desert in Mexico, about 60 km south of the Rio Grande opposite Del Rio — outside Texas and outside every other instance in the fleet, and inside permalink_gate so the app answers the click and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-11-11: TIGERweb's state layer places it in no state (controls: the State Capitol returns Texas, and a point in Chihuahua returns no state), none of the state's shipped boundary files contains it, and no outline in fleet-outlines.json does. IT IS IN ANOTHER COUNTRY, SO NO NEIGHBOUR'S GO-LIVE MOVES IT.

geometry.note: The whole-Texas outline for the coverage wash (loadMetroOutline), dissolved from the county fabric (254 counties).
The 254 counties — the instance's offline anchor layer and the ground the coverage tests use.
The 38 U.S. House districts, TIGERweb layer 4 (CD119), the map the sitting members were elected from in 2024, drawn until 3 January 2027.
The 31 Texas Senate districts, TIGERweb layer 1 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Upper).
The 150 Texas House districts, TIGERweb layer 2 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Lower).

The ZIP code search index (scripts/build_zip_index.mjs): one Point per ZIP code the app's ZIP layer draws, at the spot inside it on the layer's own ground farthest from every edge, with its extent and its layer, so a ZIP code typed into the search box selects that spot, turns the ZIP layer on and pins it for comparison (ENGINE geocoder-search, showZip). A ZIP code with no spot 75 m clear of every edge is left out, and one that crosses into another app's state is listed by whichever app holds more of it. GENERATED from data/app/tiles/zip-code.pmtiles, with each spot inside metro-outline.json (the outline its coverage test reads); --check rebuilds it from the committed archive and outline. Exact count, because it changes only when the Census Bureau changes its ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, and that wants reading rather than a widened bound.

Texas's tribal land (scripts/build_tribal_areas.py) — three reservations and three pieces of off-reservation trust land, held by three nations. The floor and the ceiling are equal because that is what the Census publishes inside the state on the current vintage, measured 2026-11-12; a change in either direction is a change in the Census's own map and wants reading rather than a widened bound.

rosters.note: U.S. House (TX) roster, refreshed weekly by update-tx-congress-roster.yml.
Texas Senate roster from the Senate's own member pages (senate.texas.gov), one record per district, refreshed weekly.
Texas House roster from the House's own member pages (house.texas.gov), one record per district, refreshed weekly.

The councils of Texas's three nations, each from its own page (the Alabama-Coushatta, the Kickapoo Traditional Tribe of Texas and the Ysleta del Sur Pueblo), keyed by the Census AIANNH code of their land — scripts/build_tribal_areas.py --rosters from data/tribal-councils.json, which scripts/tribal_council_scraper.py re-reads weekly (update-tribal-councils.yml, listed in the Wisconsin worksheet because one root workflow belongs to one instance). Merged onto tribal-areas.json by the layer's loader, so the land stays cache-first and the names network-first.
The recorded gaps this instance ships with, rendered by the data-gaps panel.

The officers Texas elects statewide and its two U.S. senators: state, officers (office, name, the office's own website, the day the name was last checked there) and usSenate. Built weekly by scripts/build_statewide_officials.py from tx/data/source/statewide-officials.source.json, which lists each office, the name and the page that must print it; the build reads robots.txt before every page, refuses to write when a page it read no longer prints the name, keeps the last checked record when a page cannot be read, and takes the senators from senate.gov's own list. Network-first: a name can change.
